research_notes: Initial research 2026-10-01: frozen and indexed parliamentary biographies, own/party profiles, official first-speech locator, business-name searches, public professional-profile search and 2017 UTS event report. Both search engines used; no relevant historical employer annual report found because early employers remain unidentified.

Full-time evidence absent. Apprenticeship and managerial titles do not establish hours; proprietor status is self-employed, not full-time by default. Published 1977-79 double listing may describe overlap or a chronology error; preserved and flagged, not silently corrected.

Employer and control follow-up: identify apprenticeship/training employer, 1979-84 manager employer, 1984-89 building employer and all own businesses. Search hit Colbeck Building Services was linked to Western Australia and not reliably the Tasmanian senator; UK business/accountant profiles and US Colbeck Capital also discarded as unverified namesakes.

First speech PDF access failed with (403) Forbidden; later targeted search explicitly returned Blocked by robots.txt (non-retryable). No retry or bypass after explicit robots error. Obtain another legitimately public reproduction or historical biography in follow-up.

2016-18 activity remains unresolved. UTS lists attendance at 18 June 2017 economic dialogue as former minister, not as a paid consultant or employee; no employment spell manufactured from event participation. Scope includes possible work during this political-career break.

Follow-up: employer identities and historical control, work dates/hours/leave; consultancy legal name and operational end; chamber presidency dates/pay; early education/employment gap; 2016-18 work. Board membership, party and elected-office roles remain excluded. More than two decades in construction is a broad career description, not a calculable full-time total.
